title: Implicit Assumptions About Tasks in Continual Learning
abstract: arXiv:2610.41792v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Continual learning is the study of how a model accumulates knowledge from data received over time, rather than all at once. In practice, this is typically achieved by dividing a dataset into tasks and presenting them sequentially. Explanations of the resulting measurements take into account factors such as the similarity between segments, the rate at which the data changes and the order of presentation. Each of these factors can be defined in terms of the underlying data, the partition imposed on it, or the learner that encounters it. These levels do not necessarily coincide, and it is usually left implicit which level a reported quantity refers to. We separate these and identify which properties acquire a value at each level. translated_title: 持续学习中关于任务的隐含假设
translated_abstract: 持续学习研究的是模型如何从随时间接收的数据（而非一次性获得的所有数据）中积累知识。在实践中，这通常通过将数据集划分为若干任务并按顺序呈现来实现。对由此产生的测量结果的解释，会考虑诸如数据段之间的相似性、数据变化的速率以及呈现顺序等因素。这些因素中的每一个都可以在三个层面来定义：底层数据本身、施加于数据之上的任务划分，或是遇到这些数据的学习者。这三个层面并不必然一致，而通常报告中并未明确说明所给出的量指的是哪个层面。我们将这些层面区分开来，并识别出哪些属性是在每个层面上获得其取值的。在受控的教师—学生实验中，我们证明了对相同的底层数据轨迹在不同粒度层级上进行划分、改变呈现顺序以及改变相似性结构……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文揭示了持续学习研究中“任务”相关测量可在底层数据、任务划分和学习者三个不同层面定义，这些层面并不必然一致，并通过教师—学生受控实验证明了不同层面的隐含假设会显著影响实验结果。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that task-based measurements in continual learning can be defined at three distinct levels—underlying data, partition, and learner—which do not necessarily coincide, and demonstrates via controlled teacher-student experiments how implicit assumptions at each level affect reported results.
